chapter: Then versus now, dances and carnival balls
title: Carnival balls with Desvigne
summary: The band played many carnival balls, including the Young Men Illinois; guests wore masks until midnight.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: When you were with Sidney Desvene, did he play many of the carnival balls for any of the carnival clubs?
We played a lot of carnival balls. They played the young men of Illinois' balls. They played...
What was the young men of Illinois? Did that be like anybody that worked for Illinois Central or something? I wonder...
How'd they call it Illinois? Where'd that come from? Maybe they liked that name. She was up there. I didn't know. I wonder. Because it was from the north, I guess they liked that name.

But they never worked for no railroad. I wonder where that name came from. They never worked for no railroad. And Sidney played a lot of carnival balls. A lot of carnival balls. I didn't know who we were playing for, but it was carnival balls.
Would people be in costume or mask or anything?

Yeah, be in costume or mask, and at 12 o'clock they would take off their mask. Yeah. That was a law. They'd be pretty gown. Some would be in devil suits. Some would be in all kinds of costume. Yeah. In masks. And you didn't know who they were until 12 o'clock. 12 o'clock comes and everybody was unmasked.
